property_summary: For any caller who is the owner and for any contract balance > 0, calling withdrawAll transfers the entire contract balance out (reducing address(c).balance to 0); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) breaks this by leaving the contract balance > 0 for some inputs.

For any caller who is the owner and any positive deposit amount sent to the contract, calling withdrawAll reduces the contract balance to zero (reference); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) leaves a positive contract balance for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any owner caller and any nonzero sequence of deposits into the contract (via fallback), after the owner calls withdrawAll the contract balance becomes equal to zero (reference); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave a positive contract balance for some inputs, so there exists a sequence of deposits and an owner such that address(c).balance != 0 after withdrawAll.

For any owner who makes at least one successful external deposit into C (so contract balance > 0), calling withdrawAll as the owner reduces address(c).balance to 0 in the reference; the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave address(c).balance > 0 for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any owner who has previously received deposits into C (so C has positive balance), calling withdrawAll as the owner transfers the entire contract balance out (address(c).balance becomes 0); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave a positive balance, violating this.
After the owner withdraws all, the balance of contract c equals zero when only the owner can withdraw.
Only the owner can successfully call withdraw: calls to withdraw by non-owners must revert.
A caller different from the contract owner (this test contract) cannot successfully call c.withdraw(1) (the call must revert).
A caller different from the contract owner (i.e., this test contract) cannot withdraw successfully; the attempted withdraw must revert.
A caller different from the contract owner (i.e., this test contract) cannot withdraw successfully; the attempted withdraw must revert.

For any caller and any call to sendMoney(target, value, data), only the contract owner can reduce the contract balance via withdraw afterwards (i.e., after sendMoney completes the contract's balance can only be reduced by owner withdrawals); the mutant removing the onlyOwner check allows a non-owner to withdraw and thus can make address(c).balance smaller for some inputs.

For any target address and value, only the contract owner can reduce the contract's balance by calling withdraw; therefore after calling sendMoney(target, value, data) (which may trigger an external call), the contract balance minus any non-sendMoney withdrawals remains equal to its prior balance minus the forwarded value when only the owner can withdraw — the mutant removing onlyOwner on withdraw allows a non-owner to later drain funds, violating that the contract's balance can only be decreased by owner-only withdrawals.

For any adversarial callee and any value forwarded via sendMoney, only the owner can subsequently reduce the contract balance by calling withdraw — i.e., after an external interaction via sendMoney the contract balance cannot be reduced by a non-owner; removing onlyOwner on withdraw allows a non-owner helper to drain funds and thus violates this property for some fuzzed value.

For every target helper with a failing fallback and any forwarded value, after the owner calls sendMoney(...) the contract's balance cannot be decreased by a non-owner calling withdraw (reference enforces withdraw onlyOwner; mutant allows any caller to withdraw and thus can decrease address(c).balance).

For every caller A and amount v that A might attempt to withdraw, the reference contract C ensures that a non-owner calling withdraw(v) reverts (so a non-owner cannot change address(c).balance); the mutant removing onlyOwner allows some non-owner to successfully withdraw and thus can make address(c).balance smaller for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and any withdraw amount where the contract has sufficient balance, the reference contract always reduces its own balance by the withdrawn amount after withdraw(...) returns; the mutant that uses send can fail to transfer (silently returning false) and thus leave the contract balance unchanged for some inputs (fuzz-found recipient behaviour/amount).
When owner asks sendMoney to forward a positive ETH amount, the target address's balance increases by exactly that amount.

For every caller, only the contract owner can make sendMoney transfer out funds (i.e., after any call to sendMoney by a non-owner the contract balance remains unchanged); the mutant that removes the onlyOwner check allows non-owners to drain funds, violating this rule for some inputs.

For all callers and calldata, only the owner can make C send value out via sendMoney, so after any sendMoney call made by a non-owner the contract balance must not decrease; the mutant that removes the onlyOwner check allows a non-owner to cause the contract balance to drop for some inputs.

For every caller and calldata, if a non-owner attempts to call sendMoney on C, the call must not cause the contract to transfer Ether out (i.e., address(c).balance does not decrease); removing the onlyOwner check allows a non-owner to trigger a transfer for some inputs, violating this rule.

For every caller address and calldata, only the owner (deployer) may cause C to transfer Ether out via sendMoney; removing the onlyOwner check lets a non-owner caller invoke sendMoney to make the contract send Ether out, which can decrease address(c).balance for some fuzzed inputs.

For all callers and calldata, calling sendMoney(...) should only succeed (i.e., not revert) if msg.sender == owner; removing the onlyOwner check allows non-owners to successfully invoke sendMoney for some inputs (the mutant makes sendMoney succeed for a non-owner while the reference would revert).
